plan: Keep all patient-facing state in one public `session` dict with exactly the four contracted keys, rebuilt from a single initial-state factory for begin/abandon resets.
Copy `appointments` (list of dict copies) at construction and precompute the set of known ids for validation.
Dispatch `handle` through a class-level table keyed by `action["type"]`; non-dict actions and unknown types short-circuit to an error screen.

Use validate-then-commit in every handler: all guards (active/incomplete session, field types, known ids, completion prerequisites) run before any mutation, so rejected actions never corrupt accepted data and never raise.
Build every screen through one factory that returns fresh `prompt`/`messages`/`choices` structures and derives appointment choices exactly when the prompt is `Choose appointment`.
Derive the post-correction prompt from a next-unmet-prompt rule: unconfirmed contact -> `Confirm contact`, no appointment -> `Choose appointment`, else `Review and complete`.

Expose input/output as injected `action_source`/`screen_sink` ports; `run_once()` raises `RuntimeError` before touching either if one is missing, then reads one action, handles it, displays the screen exactly once, and returns that same object.
mechanisms: single mutable session dictionary with an initial-state factory
constructor-time copy of appointments plus known-id set
validate-then-commit guards producing `Error:` screens without mutation
centralized screen factory with prompt-driven choice inclusion
dependency-injected action source and screen sink ports checked in run_once
